note: SPOILERS: later stages of these entries describe what each scenario's postmortem reveals. The game shows a stage only once the player has started (seen) or finished (after) that scenario.

entries.name: Kordav
entries.role: Elsin's neighbour to the north and west

stages.text: Its farmland depends on the Veyl River, which rises in Elsin. The two have argued over the water for ten years. Its 4th Army trains at Ostrel, 40 km from the border, and its Bureau runs its intelligence.
IRON HARVEST was a real exercise, enlarged to put pressure on the water talks. When the talks failed, its leadership authorised a plan to seize Tarsk Dam.
Its lead elements found a battalion dug in at Dolan and stopped at the river.
Its engineers bridged the river at Dolan and took the dam's access road. The dam is still argued over.
It holds Tarsk Dam, and calls it securing critical water infrastructure.
It sent a major on its General Staff, LANTERN, to walk into our embassy and smear Deputy Defence Minister Vell before a vote.
Blamed for the Southern Line attacks, and innocent of them: the evidence against it was planted.
The replacement terminals for Elsin's ministry spent a day and a half on a fenced quay at Brask, on Kordav's coast, and came back sealed.
Paid a criminal crew in advance to break Elsin's grid controls, so that Elsin would repair them from images on a compromised update server.
Its Bureau has read everything that crossed LATTICE for four years.

entries.bio: A large, centralised state governed from its capital by a small leadership that rarely explains itself. Its wealth is grain from the lower Veyl, which is why the river matters more to it than any border. Its coast is cold and its harbours few; Brask is the only one that matters. Its army is large, and its state broadcaster, KSB, is never off message.

entries.name: Elsin

stages.text: Holds the Veyl's headwaters and Tarsk Dam, 6 km inside the border. Hosts Task Force VEYL, and asked for months to have it at Tarsk.
Its parliament is fractious. Deputy Defence Minister Aron Vell negotiated the task force agreement, and some of Elsin's own officers distrust him.
Its gas pipeline, the Southern Line, runs from the Kessa pumping station through the Sarn valley to the Tolen bridge on the border with Marrat.
Its ministries talk to the alliance over LATTICE, a secure terminal link.
Its northern grid and the Southern Line's pumping controls run on control servers built by Corvane Systems.

entries.bio: A small, landlocked parliamentary republic of highlands and river valleys. Its governments are coalitions and its votes are close. It looks west to the alliance for its security, south to Marrat's free port at Halsk for its trade, and north at Kordav with long suspicion.

entries.name: Marrat

stages.text: Wants its border guards on the Southern Line, and already has advisers at Elsin's Southern Command.
Its intelligence service paid and armed the Sarn Valley Front for a month to frighten Elsin into a security pact, then cut it loose. When the Front turned rogue, Marrat warned Elsin, truthfully.
The pact is dead. Elsin sent its advisers home.
Its guards got the southern third of the line under a thinner pact.
Elsin signed the pact. Its guards are on the line, protecting it from a militia Marrat built.
Runs Halsk, a free port on its coast, with a rail line to Kalsa.
Innocent of the grid attack. Its language was added to the malware to make it look guilty.

entries.bio: A coastal trading state whose fortune is Halsk, a free port that handles much of the region's freight, and most of Elsin's. Its foreign policy is commercial and patient. It keeps good relations with everyone it can sell to.

entries.name: The alliance
entries.role: The multinational alliance you work for

stages.text: Keeps Task Force VEYL in Elsin to reassure it. Shares a daily assessment with Kalsa.
Runs an Infrastructure Protection Cell in Kalsa, under Director Ilse Brandt.

entries.bio: A multinational defence alliance. Elsin is a partner, not a member, and Task Force VEYL is the alliance's promise that the difference won't matter.

entries.name: Pellaria
entries.role: A neutral state to the north-east. Capital: Aubrec.

stages.text: The water talks between Kordav and Elsin were held in Aubrec.
LANTERN walked into our embassy in Aubrec. The Bureau keeps an office there, and Kordav an embassy.

entries.bio: Neutral for longer than anyone in the region can remember. Aubrec, its capital, hosts more embassies than it has ministries, most of the region's negotiations, and a metro that goes on strike most winters.

entries.name: Gen. R. Halvorsen

stages.text: Your first customer. He commits forces in proportion to your confidence, and remembers when he has had to pull them back.
Placed one guard company on the Southern Line on your word.
Copied on the damage assessment. His revised Veyl contingency plan was due in Kalsa on the 17th.

entries.bio: A career armoured officer from one of the alliance's northern members. He has commanded Task Force VEYL since it arrived in Elsin. Plain-spoken, careful with his soldiers, and allergic to moving them twice.

entries.name: Under Secretary H. Marlowe

stages.text: Handles the alliance's relationship with Elsin. She won't accuse anyone on a guess.
Advised Kalsa on what to do with the missing terminals.
Opened the damage assessment. Her High actions can't be undone, and she likes to have something to show Kalsa.

entries.bio: A career diplomat who has handled the alliance's side of the Elsin relationship for six years, the task force agreement included. She reads everything twice, and won't sign what she can't defend.

entries.name: Director Ilse Brandt

stages.text: An engineer, with no patience for estimative language. She acts only on High.

entries.bio: A power engineer who ran grid control rooms for twenty years before she ran the people who protect them. She calls estimative language "weather forecasting."

entries.name: Col. E. Rhun
entries.role: Head of the liaison desk, Elsin military intelligence (WREN)

stages.text: Her desk is the voice behind WREN.
Rude about Halsk, and right about Tessaly Freight.
A forged chat log, and then Kordav's broadcaster, pointed at "the liaison office." Her copy of the network diagram never left her safe.
Innocent. Everything that reached her desk over LATTICE could leak; nothing she received on paper ever did. She asked for a transfer.
Removed from the liaison desk at the alliance's request, on your assessment.

entries.bio: Edda Rhun has spent twenty-two years in Elsin's military intelligence, the last six running its liaison desk with the alliance. Blunt and political, she has never hidden her low opinion of Aron Vell, or of Marrat's free port.

entries.name: Maj. T. Arle
entries.role: Intelligence staff officer to Gen. Halvorsen

stages.text: Runs Halvorsen's distribution.
His lists were long, and he was on leave all January. Sloppy, and innocent.
Relieved, on your assessment.

entries.bio: Tobin Arle is Halvorsen's intelligence staff officer. Capable, overworked, and generous with distribution lists.

entries.name: Aron Vell

stages.text: Negotiated the task force agreement. Kordav's least favourite politician in Kalsa, and facing a no-confidence vote.
The target of the Bureau's smear: a ledger of forged entries built from his public schedule.
Arrested on the morning of the vote.
Resigned "to clear his name."
The motion against him failed by forty votes.
Kept his job by three votes, and lost his reputation.
Survived by five votes, without knowing who was behind it.

entries.bio: One of Kalsa's younger reformers, and the minister who negotiated the task force agreement. His enemies in parliament are numerous. His enemies in Kordav are louder.

entries.name: LANTERN
entries.role: A walk-in at our embassy in Aubrec

stages.text: Said he was a major on the planning directorate of Kordav's General Staff.
He was: a real mid-level planning officer, recruited by the Bureau for one job. He walked in on orders.

entries.bio: A cryptonym, given at the embassy within the hour. He arrived with a briefcase, a story, and a request for coffee.

entries.name: Davin Oro

stages.text: A farmer whose land was taken for the Sarn compressor station.
Marrat promised him his land back, then cut him loose. He turned on the thing he actually hated: the compressor station.
Taken alive at the quarry road, still asking about his fields.

entries.bio: A third-generation farmer in the Sarn valley. Most of his family's land went under the Sarn compressor station. The compensation came late, and short.

entries.name: O. Lind

stages.text: Deputy Director at the grid operator.
Wrote that a rebuild by hand would mean nine more days of blackouts in January, and that people would die of it. He wasn't wrong about the cold.

entries.bio: Ran Elsin's grid control rooms for fifteen years before becoming the operator's deputy director. He has seen a lot of hard winters.

stages.text: Headquartered in Kordav's capital, with an office in Aubrec.
Ran LANTERN, watched the defence ministry for anyone asking about him, and staged a recall on the headquarters net it believed we read.
Hired Grey Ledger through a front company, and planted a chat log blaming the liaison office.
Altered LATTICE's terminals in transit four years ago, and has read the link ever since. A mole hunt suited it: a hunt for a person protects an implant.

entries.name: Task Force VEYL
entries.role: The alliance's reassurance force in Elsin

stages.text: Commanded by Gen. Halvorsen. 2nd Battalion is its manoeuvre force. Its garrison is south-east of Tarsk.
Buys its fuel off the Southern Line.

entries.name: Kordav's 4th Army
entries.role: Kordav's army on the Elsin border

stages.text: Runs the annual IRON HARVEST exercise at Ostrel, supplied from the depot at Varn.
12th Brigade and 77th Engineer Regiment (bridging) left Ostrel for a hidden staging area near the Dolan crossing.

entries.name: Sarn Valley Front
entries.role: A local militia in the Sarn valley

stages.text: Claimed the explosion that damaged a valve housing on the Southern Line.
Paid and armed by Marrat for a month, then cut loose and left to act alone.
Builds secure communications hardware for Elsin's defence ministry, including the CX-4 terminals.
Built and maintains the control servers for Elsin's grid, and runs their update server.
Maintains LATTICE.
Its update server held an image set built two days before the attack, carrying a component that isn't on its build list.
Honest throughout. It didn't know what was in its own terminals.
Was to put the container of terminals on a train to Kalsa.
Kordav's forwarder. Its chartered coaster took the container to Brask and back, and its owner's private crew stowed it in a shed customs had already searched.
Also shipped LATTICE's original terminals to Kalsa, four years ago, 36 hours late.
Nineteen victims in three years, always for money. Claimed the attack on Elsin's grid.
Hired for this one, paid in advance, told which six servers to hit and told not to close.

entries.name: Infrastructure Protection Cell
entries.role: The alliance's infrastructure security office in Kalsa

stages.text: Run by Director Brandt. Its forensic team, IPC LAB, is careful and slower than anyone would like.

entries.name: LATTICE
entries.role: The secure terminal link between the alliance and Elsin's ministries

stages.text: The alliance's link to Elsin's ministries. Liaison requests to Kalsa go over it.
Compromised. Its terminals were altered during a 36-hour delay in Halsk four years ago. Only what crossed it ever leaked.
Shut, on your assessment.
Still running.
Kordav's state television and official channels. Says what Kordav wants said.

entries.name: WREN

stages.text: A long relationship. Pushes what it wants us to see, and answers requests.
Its unsourced claim on the first day of the Southern Line was true.

entries.bio: The alliance's oldest liaison channel with Elsin's military intelligence, older than the task force. It tells you what Elsin wants you to know, and what you ask, in that order.

entries.name: KESTREL
entries.role: A clerk at 4th Army's depot in Varn

stages.text: Sees allocations, issue orders and accounting codes, not unit plans. Don't meet him two days running.

entries.bio: A clerk at the fuel and supply depot in Varn, recruited eight months before IRON HARVEST. He counts things, and he is very good at counting things.

entries.name: FINCH

stages.text: Six years, reliable. Meetings take two days to arrange, and the ministry is a dangerous place to ask questions.

entries.bio: Six years inside Kordav's defence ministry. Never late, never asks for more money, and never meets in a hurry.

entries.name: MAGPIE
entries.role: A fuel trader in the Sarn valley

stages.text: Sells to the Front. Sees their money and their vehicles, not their plans.

entries.bio: Sells diesel and gas oil up and down the Sarn valley, to anyone who pays in cash. The Front pays in cash.

entries.name: GANNET

stages.text: Sees what moves through the bonded sheds at night.

entries.bio: Night foreman at Halsk's bonded sheds, recruited weeks before the shipment went missing. Sees what moves, and when.

entries.name: PETREL

stages.text: Has dealt with Grey Ledger, and hears what the crew complains about.

entries.bio: Brokers stolen data on criminal forums. Talks to us because we pay well and ask nothing about the rest of his business.

entries.name: Imre Vasko

stages.text: Writes one note a day.
Anchors on his first theory, and reads everything after it that way.

entries.bio: A regional analyst with a decade on the Kordav desk. He knows the country's politics by heart, and forms a view early.

entries.name: Noor Halden

stages.text: Signals, imagery and forensics.
Slow but careful, and never wrong. Her notes arrive a day after the item.

entries.bio: A technical analyst: signals, imagery and forensics. She checks everything twice, and it shows in her timing.

entries.name: Tess Marrow

stages.text: Joined the cell for the Southern Line.
Overconfident, and occasionally sharp.
Flagged by vetting for travel she declared late. It was her mother's funeral.
Suspended pending review.

entries.bio: An open-source analyst who joined the cell from a commercial due-diligence firm. Quick, confident, and very good at finding things online.

offmap.text: Pellaria and Aubrec, to the north-east ↗
